best_parts: node S3.ret: three models in one vignette (spell, improvement, heart failure) with keys balanced to the shortest option; the mother's 'last week/today' cue makes the spell case the only one that uses the mechanism.

nodes S4.f3 -> S4.f3_ok / S4.f3_t1 / S4.f3_t2: the 'may classically' key is hedged, the stem is neutral, and the trap feedback names the superlative ('always present') as the model. A good template for E4.
nodes S4.t3 -> S4.t3_ok -> S4.t2 -> S4.t4: probe first, then the explanation, then a contrast probe. The order the refine plan asked for.
node S5.m1_expl: names both wrong readings ('improvement' and 'failing left ventricle') and explains the murmur with the flow mechanism. Good for TR8/TR11 together.
nodes S5.a2 -> S5.a3 -> S5.b1: worked case A, then case B done by the learner. Fading from worked example to learner-owned step.
nodes S7.m5 / S7.m6 / S7.m8: classmate-correction probes where each wrong correction is one trap and the feedback names the model. The best form in the module for TR12/TR17/TR22.

report section: each trap has avoided / fell_recovered / fell_open text, each objective has secure / shaky / gap text, and calibration and help patterns are present. The per-trap fell_open lines point at a card.
